newsitem.title: POLAND: Warta gets PLN 60 mln flood damage claims.
newsitem.headline: Warta gets PLN 60 mln flood damage claims.

text.p: The Polish insurer Warta has received 60 million zlotys ($17.4 million) worth of flood damage claims and has already paid out around one million zlotys, its spokesman said on Friday.
"Until now there has been a total of 60 million zlotys of flood damage claims and we have already paid out around 990,000 zlotys," Zbigniew Augustynowicz told Reuters.

Warta's president told a news conference that the company estimated it would receive a total of 160 million zlotys worth of damage claims in relation to the flooding which inundated more than 6,000 sq km in south-western Poland.
"Our estimates of total flood damage claims amount to 160 million zlotys," Andrzej Witkowski said.
Witkowski said the claims would not affect the company's financial stability or earnings for 1997 as the company was reinsured in about 70 leading European reinsurance firms.
"The entire amount of damages is thoroughly reinsured. Warta has 80-percent reinsurance coverage in top European companies," Witkowski said.
Witkowski said the company's results for the first half of the year would be released in early August and the expected net profit of 26 million zlotys was plausible.

He also said that despite the flooding, Warta introduced new products in the second half of the year, like new car damage calculation system, new forms of flat and building insurance and travel insurance for firms.
